title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Manufacturing
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Manufacturing took 747 of 1,140 industrial ransomware hits last quarter — and not one attacker touched a PLC
items.content_text: Dragos counted 1,140 ransomware incidents at industrial organizations in the second quarter, up 12% from 1,020 in Q1, and manufacturing absorbed 747 of them — 65% of the total. Construction added 176 and equipment manufacturing 114; ICS-adjacent firms including engineering companies and system integrators accounted for 117, and food and beverage 70. North America led with 514 incidents, Europe 316. The finding that should shape plant planning is a negative one: Dragos observed no case during the quarter in which a ransomware operator directly manipulated an industrial control system. Production stopped anyway. The damage ran through IT, ERP and virtualization — scheduling, material movement, order execution and the hypervisors hosting MES and historian servers. For most plants the realistic scenario is not encrypted PLCs but an ERP that cannot tell the line what to build.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Dragos Industrial Ransomware Analysis Q2 2026; Help Net Security

items.title: Federal advisory: attackers are using TIA Portal, Studio 5000 and EcoStruxure to rewrite PLC logic
items.content_text: The 22 July update to joint advisory AA26-097A describes exactly the toolchain a controls engineer uses. Iran-affiliated actors connect to internet-exposed controllers with the vendors’ own software — Rockwell Studio 5000 Logix Designer, Schneider EcoStruxure Control Expert and Siemens TIA Portal — over ports 44818, 2222, 102, 502 and 22, from leased third-party infrastructure. They extract and exfiltrate project files, then modify and delete logic. In one US case the FBI found a downloaded project file that preserved ladder logic for downstream function while adding logic overriding the instruction sets that maintained safe operating parameters, and disabling shutdown and alarm logic so equipment could enter unsafe states silently. Named targets now include Rockwell CompactLogix and Micro850, Schneider Modicon M340 (BMX P34) and Siemens S7-1200 — the standard fleet on a discrete or process line.

_otthreatfeed.date_note: Updated 22 Jul 2026 (originally published 7 Apr 2026) — campaign ongoing

items.title: Coca-Cola halted US production at fairlife after ransomware reached production-related systems
items.content_text: Coca-Cola disclosed on 16 July that its fairlife dairy subsidiary identified unauthorized third-party access to part of its systems, including production-related systems, in connection with a ransomware event, and that production operations at fairlife in the United States were temporarily suspended as a result. Reporting on the incident centred on the ERP layer carrying scheduling, material movement and order execution — the same dependency Dragos identifies as the main disruption path across the sector. It is the cleanest recent example of a plant losing output without an attacker ever addressing a controller, and it happened at an operator with resources far beyond a typical mid-market manufacturer.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Coca-Cola disclosure; Cybersecurity Dive, TechCrunch, Industrial Cyber
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Disclosed 16 Jul 2026 — US production temporarily suspended

items.title: Six agencies publish Gunra ransomware advisory; manufacturing among the named victim sectors
items.content_text: Joint advisory AA26-222A, released 10 August by CISA, the FBI, DC3, NSA, the Secret Service and South Korea’s National Police Agency, covers Gunra ransomware. Gunra emerged in April 2025 built on leaked Conti source code and has since become a ransomware-as-a-service operation recruiting affiliates through dark-web forums. Affiliates break in through exposed edge infrastructure — VPN gateways, firewall appliances and RDP-reachable systems — and run double extortion, exfiltrating before encrypting. Manufacturing, transport, utilities and government are among the named victim sectors. The entry-point list matters more than the family name: the same appliance that lets a machine-builder dial in for support is the documented way in.

items.title: Claroty finds 23 flaws in Copeland XWEB Pro controllers that chain to root — and a hidden login in Danfoss AK-SM 800A
items.content_text: Claroty’s Team82 disclosed 23 vulnerabilities in Copeland XWEB Pro supervisory refrigeration controllers, 21 of them high severity, which can be chained — authentication flaws plus predictable administrator credentials plus command injection — to bypass security controls and achieve root-level remote code execution. In a separate disclosure the team found three flaws in Danfoss AK-SM 800A controllers, including a hidden ‘code-of-the-day’ authentication mechanism that can be abused to bypass normal login and reach code execution. In a demonstration, a compromised controller remotely manipulated cooling fans and compressors while concealing the resulting temperature rise from operators. Copeland shipped firmware 1.13 and Danfoss R4.3.1. For process manufacturers the lesson generalises beyond refrigeration: facilities-purchased supervisory controllers on chillers, compressors and air handling sit on plant networks with web management enabled and no controls-engineering oversight.

_otthreatfeed.date_note: Published week of 10–14 Aug 2026; vendor fixes released

items.title: 4,407 controllers found answering EtherNet/IP on the public internet
items.content_text: A Shodan query run on 3 August returned 4,407 devices exposing port 44818, with roughly 65% in the United States, 12% in Canada and 3% in Spain. The research was prompted by the water-sector attacks, and of 22 controllers located in affected cities, 19 were on firmware susceptible to CVE-2017-16740 — a Modbus TCP buffer overflow in Rockwell MicroLogix 1400 Series B and C on firmware 21.002 and earlier, fixed in 21.003. Manufacturers rarely believe this applies to them, and the exposure usually is not the main plant: it is a machine builder’s remote-support router at a satellite line, a leased packaging skid with its own SIM, or a controller a contractor put on a DMZ during commissioning and nobody removed.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Forescout Vedere Labs analysis; The Hacker News
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Shodan scan data 3 Aug 2026 — reported week of 3–7 Aug 2026

items.title: CVSS 10 unauthenticated root command injection in Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway — critical manufacturing named
items.content_text: CISA released 14 ICS advisories on 13 August, led by CVE-2026-19188 in the Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway at CVSS 10.0. The device’s ‘Net Check’ feature passes user-supplied input from the cmdPing Socket.io event to the operating system without sanitizing it, letting an unauthenticated remote attacker execute arbitrary OS commands as root with no user interaction. Version 3.40.1.12 is affected, and CISA names critical manufacturing alongside energy and water among the deployment sectors. These combined HMI/gateway/DTU units are the low-cost remote-monitoring boxes that arrive attached to OEM machinery, leased equipment and small packaging or ancillary lines — the tier of asset that is bought on a capex line rather than through controls engineering and rarely appears in a patch cycle.

items.title: August ICS Patch Tuesday: maximum-severity authentication bypass in Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050, plus CAD and simulation fixes
items.content_text: Siemens published 10 advisories on 11 August. The headline is a maximum-severity missing-authentication flaw in SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices (SSA-834709) that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with elevated privileges. A critical code-execution flaw was fixed in Siveillance Video Management Servers, and high-severity issues in Solid Edge, Simcenter Nastran, the Siemens License Server, Simcenter Femap, Parasolid and Logo! Soft Comfort — the CAD, CAE and licensing stack sitting on engineering desktops, exploitable to crash applications, execute code, elevate privileges or read arbitrary files. Medium-severity fixes landed in Ruggedcom devices and Desigo controllers. Schneider Electric covered NetBotz 5 and PowerChute Serial Shutdown; Phoenix Contact addressed multiple PLCnext firmware flaws exploitable without authentication; Honeywell issued several building-management advisories.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Siemens ProductCERT, Schneider Electric, Phoenix Contact and Honeywell PSIRT via SecurityWeek

items.title: Cisco Secure Firewall ASA/FTD zero-day added to CISA KEV after denial-of-service exploitation
items.content_text: CISA added three vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 11 August, including CVE-2026-20349, a heap-inspection flaw in Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance and Firewall Threat Defense that Cisco patched after it was exploited as a zero-day for denial-of-service attacks. The others are a use-after-free in the Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock (CVE-2026-68820) and SQL injection in Metabase (CVE-2026-72898). Earlier in the month CISA added Progress LoadMaster CVE-2026-8037 and Langflow, Apache Tomcat and N-able N-central flaws. ASA and FTD appliances commonly form the boundary between enterprise and plant networks and terminate the VPNs machine builders use; the Gunra advisory names exactly this class of device as an entry point, which makes patching it a plant-availability issue rather than an IT chore.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalog additions, 5, 7 and 11 Aug 2026
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Cisco ASA/FTD added to KEV 11 Aug 2026
